title: Cash Caregiver Rails: Deductible, Reimbursable, Legal
one_liner: Payroll plus clinician plan-of-care paperwork that turns cash-paid family and neighbor caregivers into tax-deductible, insurance-reimbursable, workers'-comp-covered employment.
customer: Adult children and spouses who pay $15-30 an hour in cash to informal home aides for a parent with dementia, frailty or serious illness. The households spend $20-60K a year, and some have long-term care insurance.
problem: A large slice of elder home care runs on cash, word of mouth and no paperwork. Families lose tax deductions and long-term care insurance benefits that require documentation. They carry unlimited liability for injuries in their home and owe unpaid household-employer taxes. The aide has no wage record, comp cover, or path to benefits. Agencies solve this at $35+ an hour, which many families can't afford.
solution: An employer-of-record service for family-hired caregivers. It provides payroll, tax filing (household employer) and workers' comp or injury cover. A telehealth nurse practitioner certifies chronic illness and writes a plan of care, which are the tax and long-term care insurance requirements for 'qualified long-term care services'. A claims-ready packet is generated for long-term care insurers and the family's tax preparer, and a shift-check-in log is kept. Optional backup-aide pool for absences.
why_now: Boomers are in their 80s. Agency costs keep rising, and 2025-26 Medicaid funding cuts push more families toward informal care. Telehealth nurse practitioner visits make chronic-illness certification cheap. Household payroll rails and workers'-comp programs for single-worker households are now easy to embed through APIs.
revenue_model: $99-149 per household per month platform fee plus payroll processing. An annual $150-250 clinician certification fee. An insurer-paid fee, or employer benefit contract, for claim-ready documentation that reduces fraud and denial disputes. Backup-aide shifts at a margin.
non_obvious_insight: Families don't pay for compliance. They pay when the paperwork unlocks money that is currently being left on the table: deductions and insurance benefits that are only available to a documented, plan-of-care relationship. The clinician certification is the wedge, and payroll is just plumbing. Selling it as 'get reimbursed' rather than 'stay legal' changes conversion completely. It also builds a data asset that insurers will pay for.
first_30_days: Partner with a tax-preparer network or elder-law attorneys and geriatric care managers who see cash caregivers daily. Contract a telehealth nurse practitioner group for plan-of-care certifications. Use an existing household payroll provider under white-label. Sign 15 families at $99/month with a money-back guarantee tied to documented reimbursements. Measure recovered dollars per household as the headline metric.

title: Notary-Witnessed Hiring Against Deepfake Candidates
one_liner: On-demand licensed notaries sit beside a remote candidate for the final interview or day-one onboarding and sign an attestation.
customer: Security and talent leads at remote-first software, fintech and defence-contractor employers, plus technical recruiting agencies, staffing firms and employer-of-record providers.
problem: An August 2026 eleven-nation advisory warned that North Korean IT-worker operations use real-time deepfakes to beat hiring checks, with 6,500+ similar cases reported globally. Employers face sanctions exposure. Liveness and document checks are being defeated, and the only alternatives are flying candidates in or trusting software.
solution: A marketplace and quality layer over existing mobile notaries and I-9 authorised representatives. A candidate books a witnessed final round in their own city. The witness checks ID, sweeps the room and desk for second screens and earpieces, positions a second camera, and signs a sealed attestation. An optional witnessed live-coding session runs on a locked, company-supplied laptop. A second 10-minute witnessed check at day 30 confirms identity continuity. Coverage starts in 200 US metros and expands to the UK and EU.
why_now: Real-time deepfake interviews are now mainstream and the 11-nation advisory (Aug 2026) is prompting boards to act. The DHS remote I-9 alternative procedure already blesses human 'authorised representatives'. Mobile signing agents lost volume when mortgage origination slumped, so witness supply is cheap.
revenue_model: $150-350 per witnessed session (about 60% to the witness), $2-10k per month enterprise subscriptions, and a per-hire fee for staffing agencies.
non_obvious_insight: Insiders think software has to beat deepfakes. For high-stakes moments, the cheapest defence is physics. A $200 human in the room costs less than one failed hire, and the scarce input is legally recognised people who already verify identity for a living. There are millions of commissioned US notaries.
first_30_days: Sign 40 notaries and loan-signing agents in five metros through signing-agent communities. Write a witness protocol and kit checklist, with legal review of what a notary may attest outside a notarial act. Pilot with three staffing firms or security-conscious startups.

title: Consolidation Shock Radar for Independent Clinics
one_liner: Every roll-up creates a wave of unhappy clients and departing staff near the acquired clinic; sell independents, would-be founders and lenders a radar that finds those neighborhoods first.
customer: Independent and affordable-care clinics (client win-back and recruiting), DVMs leaving corporate to open practices, and practice lenders or equipment lessors.
problem: GoodVets is buying WellHaven (75 to 116 locations, announced 2026-09-24), and Mars runs about 2,100 clinics. After a deal, prices, hours and staffing change, but nearby independents have no signal about where clients and staff are becoming loose. De novo founders pick sites by gut feel and lenders lack local competitive data.
solution: Track acquisitions using state facility records, Google Business Profile and website changes ('now part of...'), price-list scrapes, review-sentiment shifts and job-posting churn. Deliver (a) an alert plus a ready-to-send 'neighbor clinic' welcome campaign and records-transfer kit for independents within 5 miles, (b) recruiting lists of departing DVMs and techs, and (c) site-scoring reports for lenders and de novo founders.
why_now: Continuous roll-ups (GoodVets/WellHaven this week), visits reportedly falling three years running, and corporate chains structurally unable to cut price. Open web data plus LLM extraction makes the tracking cheap for a two-person team.
revenue_model: $199-499 per month per clinic by radius, $2-5K per de novo site report, and a lender API subscription.
non_obvious_insight: Consolidation is discussed as a scale story. The neglected consequence is local displacement: the buyer's own integration changes service and pricing at a known date, which opens a recurring window for competitors. That window is a sellable time-series signal nobody packages.
first_30_days: Build scrapers for 3 states. Identify 30 clinics acquired in the last 12 months. Cold-email 100 independents within 5 miles with a 'your neighborhood's acquired clinics' one-pager. Aim to sell 5 subscriptions at $299 per month.

title: PFAS Land-Application History Reports for Farmland
one_liner: A 'Phase I environmental site assessment' for PFAS on farmland, built from biosolids land-application records and upstream discharger data, sold to lenders, farmland funds and appraisers before the sensors exist.
customer: Farm Credit associations and ag banks, farmland investment funds, rural appraisers and title firms, and farmers or buyers who need to show a field is clean.
problem: EPA released Draft Guidance for Reducing Risk from PFOA and PFOS in Biosolids on July 1, 2026, noting that sewage sludge may carry PFAS from industrial dischargers, landfills and homes. Yet EPA's own FY2026 SBIR Phase I topics still ask small businesses to invent 'Treatment of PFAS in Wastewater Sewage Sludge and Biosolids' and 'Sensors to Detect PFAS in Environmental Matrices', so cheap field screening does not exist. Lenders and buyers are pricing farmland today with no way to know whether a field received sludge, from which plant, and with what upstream industrial inputs.
solution: A desktop screening report per parcel. It combines state biosolids land-application permits and site reports (obtained by scraping and automated public-records requests), the treatment plant's upstream industrial dischargers, soil and hydrology data, and a risk tier. Higher tiers trigger a sampling plan run by a partner lab using EPA Method 1633. Deliver in the lender's existing environmental-diligence workflow, and later offer an API.
why_now: The July 1, 2026 EPA draft guidance turns PFAS in biosolids from a research topic into something lenders must ask about. EPA's Sept 24, 2026 SBIR solicitation ($100k per Phase I, 6 months, closes Nov 8, 2026) is paying for the sensing tools, so cheap field tests are years away and records-based screening is the only option now.
revenue_model: $400 to $1,200 per desktop parcel report. $2k to $6k with coordinated sampling (margin on lab work). $20k to $60k per year API or portfolio subscriptions for lenders and farmland funds.
non_obvious_insight: The government is paying to invent PFAS sensors that don't exist yet, but the lend/buy/insure decision is being made now on paper records, so the winning product is the record-linkage layer, not the sensor. EPA's FY2026 SBIR Phase I topics list 1B (PFAS in sewage sludge and biosolids) and 2A (PFAS sensors in environmental matrices), $100,000 and 6 months each: https://www.epa.gov/sbir/how-apply-sbir-contract. EPA's biosolids page lists the July 1, 2026 Draft Guidance and states that sludge may carry PFAS from upstream dischargers: https://www.epa.gov/biosolids. Lenders already require site assessments for gas stations and dry cleaners, and a PFAS-on-farmland version is the missing sibling. Caveat: the EPA pages I could fetch gave no land-application tonnage or state-by-state record availability, so records access must be checked before committing to a state.
first_30_days: Pick 1 or 2 states where biosolids land-application permits are public (verify first). Assemble records for the 20 largest treatment plants and build 25 sample reports on real parcels. Approach 5 Farm Credit associations, 3 farmland funds and 5 rural appraisers with a free report on a parcel they already own or are underwriting. Sign a lab partner for sampling. Close the first 3 paid pilots at $400 to $1,200 per parcel.

title: Live Read-Aloud Rooms Staffed by Displaced Narrators
one_liner: Landline-friendly live group reading sessions led by professional audiobook narrators for isolated and low-vision elders, sold to agencies as a human alternative to free AI companion robots, with an attested 'human minutes' ledger.
customer: Area Agencies on Aging and state aging offices, senior-living operators, and Medicare Advantage or Medicaid plans buying social-isolation supplemental benefits. Families and libraries for the blind are a secondary channel.
problem: NY, FL and NJ now hand out ElliQ AI companions free, and 'loneliness reduction' is a funded policy goal, yet the buyer is buying synthetic contact. Meanwhile professional audiobook narrators are being squeezed by AI narration programs. Many isolated elders are on landlines, have low vision or fading attention, and cannot use apps or long-form video.
solution: Dial-in or smart-speaker reading rooms, 45 minutes each, 25-40 elders per room, with rooms by taste (mysteries, poetry, serialized novels, local history, faith). The narrator addresses listeners by name and takes requests. The platform logs attendance and issues a funder-facing 'verified live human minutes' report, which is the metric that a loneliness grant or plan benefit actually needs. Shared reading has a track record in dementia settings, so a memory-care track is included.
why_now: Governments are already in the market for loneliness tech and have discretionary budgets. AI narration has pushed skilled, warm voices into part-time work exactly as human-made is turning into a priced attribute. Older adults are adopting AI fast (23% of 65+ use ChatGPT), and a visible human alternative is a differentiator for buyers under pressure not to replace people with robots.
revenue_model: $35-45 per active elder per month, priced against ElliQ's $40 a month plus $250 upfront. Narrators earn about $45 per session, and a 30-person room yields roughly 40% gross margin. Contracts come from AAA and plan budgets on annual terms.
non_obvious_insight: The funder's real KPI is human contact minutes, not content. AI companions cannot honestly claim that ledger, but a narrator-led room can prove it. The scarce input is warm, trained voices, and AI has just made a pool of them cheap and underemployed.
first_30_days: Recruit 8 narrators from audiobook narrator communities and voice-actor unions. Run 3 free public rooms via a conference bridge and recruit elders through two county AAAs and a senior center. Collect attendance and self-reported loneliness scores and pitch the county AAA a $6-10k, three-month paid pilot.

title: Hardening Passport: Proof That Earns Premium Credits
one_liner: A contractor-paid evidence layer that turns every roof, vent and 5-ft-zone job into an insurer-acceptable credit claim or parcel-score appeal.
customer: Roofing, vent-retrofit and defensible-space contractors (5-50 crews) in Colorado and California, paying per verified job. Homeowners get the packet bundled with the work.
problem: Insiders assume mitigation credits fail because insurers do not want to give them. Colorado HB25-1182 (in force July 1 2026) now forces disclosure of the parcel score, credit for documented mitigation and an appeal. But homeowners cannot produce insurer-grade proof. One owner reports 'a thousand bucks' off after a $75,000 metal roof, and Boulder's rebate is capped at $500. Contractors lose sales because the payback cannot be shown.
solution: A phone capture flow for crews: geotagged before/after photos, roof class and vent model certificates, 5-ft clearance measurements, all mapped to IBHS Wildfire Prepared Home criteria and each carrier's credit form. It outputs a ready-to-file credit packet and, in Colorado, an appeal letter citing the disclosed score. Contractors use it as a sales line ('we file your discount').
why_now: HB25-1182 took effect July 1 2026 and California AB 75 became operative the same day. IBHS Wildfire Prepared Home just expanded to Washington. This is the first time a statute gives proof a place to land.
revenue_model: $49-99 per verified job or $199/month per crew. Later, carriers pay per accepted credit, and verified-hardening portfolio data is sold to carriers and reinsurers.
non_obvious_insight: Scoring is commoditizing (MSCI paid only $120M cash for First Street), but neutral proof is still scarce. Insurers cannot advocate for the policyholder, so the party with the incentive and the field access is the contractor.
first_30_days: Sign 5 Front Range roofers or mitigation crews. Build the capture flow as a web app around the IBHS checklist. Hand-assemble 50 packets, file them with 3 carriers, and track the acceptance rate as the core proof metric.

title: Paper-Mill Shield for Diamond Open-Access Journals
one_liner: An Open Journal Systems plugin and service that screens incoming manuscripts and reviewers using public research detectors, and hands volunteer editors a plain-language decision memo.
customer: Library-publishing programs, university presses, national journal platforms and scholarly societies that run dozens to thousands of small journals on Open Journal Systems (OJS). The buyer is the consortium or library publishing unit, not the individual journal, whose budget is close to zero.
problem: Paper mills, LLM-generated manuscripts and fake reviewer identities hit small journals run by volunteer editors. Big publishers have enterprise integrity suites (Clear Skies, the STM Integrity Hub). Small journals have nothing, and a single wave of fraudulent papers can get them delisted from Scopus or Web of Science.
solution: Submission-time screening chained from public sources: Problematic Paper Screener fingerprints (tortured phrases, ChatGPT tells), reference-list checks against the Retraction Watch database now openly available through Crossref, citation-cartel and author-network anomalies via OpenAlex, and reviewer-suggestion checks (ORCID, email domain and institution mismatches). Flagged items go to a human integrity analyst. The editor receives a one-page memo with evidence and a suggested action, not a score. Includes a backlist audit product.
why_now: Paper-mill scale is now documented (the Problematic Paper Screener scans on the order of 130M publications weekly and has fed 1,000+ retractions). Retraction Watch data went open via Crossref. LLM text makes fakes cheap. Diamond open access is growing fast because of funder mandates, which means more volunteer-run journals with no integrity budget.
revenue_model: USD 3-10 per screened submission for individual journals. Consortium plans at USD 2-15k per year covering a platform's journals. Fixed-fee backlist audits per journal. Human analyst escalations billed hourly.
non_obvious_insight: The detectors already exist as free tools used by sleuths. What editors lack is accountability packaging: a defensible written memo they can cite when rejecting an author, and someone to escalate to. Sell decision memos to the consortium that hosts the journals, not detection scores to journals.
first_30_days: Build the pipeline as a command-line tool first, then an OJS plugin. Approach three library publishing programs and the PKP community forum. Offer 5 free backlist audits to journals that consent to anonymized findings. Publish a 'state of small-journal fraud' write-up from the audits as the PR hook. Sign one consortium pilot at a nominal fee.

title: Guaranteed Midday Walker as Apartment Amenity
one_liner: Sell apartment operators a fixed on-site walker window as a renewal and lease-up amenity, with residents paying a discounted per-walk fee and the building paying a retainer.
customer: Owners and property managers of 150 to 500 unit multifamily buildings in dense metros, paying a monthly retainer. Residents are the secondary payers.
problem: A solo walker loses 35 to 45 percent of the paid day to driving between homes, parking, and building lobbies. Buildings, meanwhile, pay quietly for dogs: barking and noise complaints, damage from anxious dogs, waste on the property, and hidden-dog lease violations. Pet owners renew at higher rates than other tenants, but it is hard to monetize them with pet rent, especially where fees are capped or scrutinized.
solution: A walker holds fixed weekday windows (for example 11am to 2pm and 5 to 7pm) in the building, using the fob and package room. Residents book by QR code or text, and the walker walks compatible dogs from nearby floors in groups of 3 to 4 (dog compatibility is something a walker learns quickly), with a lobby handoff. Yield per hour roughly doubles or triples versus door-to-door, so residents pay about $12 to $15 per walk instead of $25 to $30. The building gets a monthly report on walks completed, incidents, and waste-bag use, plus marketing copy ('guaranteed midday walk') for lease-up and renewals. I could not confirm in this session whether a comparable product already operates at scale, so check competitors first.
why_now: Return-to-office mandates put more dogs alone midday. Big multifamily supply waves in many metros mean operators compete on concessions and retention, and are shifting amenity spend from gyms to services. Pet-fee restrictions in some states and cities push operators to bundle services instead of charging rent. Simple text-and-QR booking removes the back-office cost that used to make this unprofitable.
revenue_model: Building retainer of roughly $1,500 to $3,000 a month for guaranteed windows, plus resident per-walk fees of $12 to $15, plus optional add-ons (waste station servicing, dog-friendly move-in tours). Expand by selling to regional operators as a portfolio amenity program.
non_obvious_insight: The walker's real margin killer is geography, not demand. A walker's hourly income is decided by drive time and cancellations, so the fix is to put demand where the walker already is. What operators really buy is not walks, it is fewer noise complaints and higher pet-owner renewals, so price it against retention, not against Rover.
first_30_days: Start with a building where you already walk two or three dogs. Ask those residents to introduce you to the community manager. Pitch a 60-day pilot at about $750 a month with walk windows and a resident-sign-up QR poster. Measure sign-ups and complaints, then take the numbers to two more buildings in the same operator or neighborhood.

title: Buy Oil-Heat Dealers, Sell Heat Pumps
one_liner: Acquire retiring Northeast heating-oil dealers for their loyal customers and boiler-failure moments, run the fuel business as a cash annuity, and convert customers to heat pumps.
customer: Northeast homeowners heating with oil (from about 19% of homes in New York to 59% in Maine), income-qualified households with state and utility rebates, and dealer owners who want a succession exit.
problem: Oil-only dealers face policy-driven volume decline and aging owners with no successors, yet each holds 1,000 to 5,000 loyal customers with known equipment ages. Heat pump installers pay high customer-acquisition costs and lack trust. The federal 25C credit ended for systems placed in service after 2025, so state programs and CAC decide winners.
solution: Acquire small dealers, keep the local brand, drivers and techs. AI ops: a propensity model using tank size, burner age, delivery volume and home age to time an offer when a boiler is about to fail, virtual site surveys and load calcs from photos, automated rebate and financing paperwork, retraining of drivers and technicians for heat pump service, and route optimization to protect fuel cash flow during the transition. Sell 'heat-as-a-service' subscriptions with dual-fuel backup.
why_now: Post-2025, incentives shifted to state and utility programs (Massachusetts, New York, Maine and others), and HEEHRA rebates of up to $8,000 for income-qualified households continue where states have launched. Heat pump technology is mature for cold climates. Dealer owners are aging, and the customer relationship is the hard-to-buy asset.
revenue_model: Fuel margin as the cash cow, service contracts, heat pump installs at roughly $15k to $25k per job, and financing spreads. Acquisition financed with seller notes and SBA 7(a).
non_obvious_insight: Electrification's scarce asset is trust plus the moment a boiler dies. Oil dealers already own both, and they are the only local business that knows each home's system age and gets the 2 a.m. January call. Buy the relationship and use the declining fuel business to fund the conversion.
first_30_days: List 50 independent dealers within a two-hour radius from state oilheat associations. Approach five owners over 60 with seller-financed offers. Before buying, start as a white-label heat pump conversion partner that rev-shares with dealers on their customers, which can produce first revenue in 60 to 90 days.

title: Recall-Proofing Subscription for Small Pet Food Brands
one_liner: Outsourced food-safety plans, pooled H5N1/Salmonella/Listeria testing and label review for the hundreds of small raw, freeze-dried and topper brands that cannot afford a QA department.
customer: Small raw, freeze-dried, topper and mixer brands and their co-packers, including Shopify-native brands.
problem: FDA now requires makers of cat and dog food using uncooked or unpasteurized poultry, dairy or egg ingredients to reanalyze their food safety plans for H5N1 under the animal-food preventive controls rule, after cats died from contaminated raw food. A recall can kill a small brand, and the fast-growing topper and mixer category (purchases +214% since 2018 per the briefing) creates label and 'complete and balanced' compliance ambiguity.
solution: A monthly subscription with PCQI-qualified plan writing and upkeep, supplier verification, a pooled testing program at negotiated lab prices with a certificate-of-analysis dashboard, mock-recall drills and label review against current AAFCO and state rules. Bundle with a recall-insurance partner for lower premiums.
why_now: FDA's H5N1 reanalysis requirement (announced January 2025) turned a news event into a permanent compliance line item. DTC consolidation (Farmer's Dog's first acquisition) raises supplier-diligence standards for small brands seeking exits.
revenue_model: $500-2,000 per month subscription, 20-30% margin on pooled testing pass-through, and insurance referral fees.
non_obvious_insight: Insiders treat H5N1 as an outbreak headline. For small brands it is a permanent, recurring cost, and testing volume can be pooled across many brands to get lab prices and QA depth no single brand can afford, the same economics that supports outsourced food-safety consultants in human food.
first_30_days: List 300 raw and freeze-dried brands from FDA registration and social listings. Send a free H5N1 gap audit against FDA's reanalysis requirement. Contract a PCQI consultant and one accredited lab. Convert 5-10 brands to paid subscriptions.

title: Financial-Aid Overflow Desk for New Loan Caps
one_liner: A managed service plus software that classifies programs as professional versus graduate, tracks lifetime caps and prevents mis-awards at small colleges' aid offices.
customer: Financial-aid directors and CFOs at small and mid-size, graduate-heavy private colleges and health-sciences schools.
problem: The July 1, 2026 regime capped grad loans at $20.5k a year and $100k total, gave only 11 'professional' programs $50k and $200k, and capped and prorated Parent PLUS by credit load. Final guidance came in May, vendors were not ready in August, and some disbursements ran 6 weeks late with no recourse. Errors create audit findings and student harm.
solution: An aid-regime desk: a program-classification dossier per program, cap tracking across borrowers including transfers, a Parent PLUS proration calculator, packaging letters, and a student-facing 'what you can borrow and alternatives' guide (private loan comparison, employer sponsorship, payment plan). Add a late-disbursement bridge program and audit-ready records.
why_now: This is the first aid cycle under the new rules. A pending healthcare-association lawsuit (December 2026 suspension deadline) means rules could change again, and vendors lag.
revenue_model: $25-90k per institution per year depending on graduate enrollment, plus bridge-loan fees per student.
non_obvious_insight: Every rule change is a compliance tax that lands hardest on small offices. The vendor lag is a 12-18 month window in which a service desk becomes embedded in the workflow and later converts to software.
first_30_days: Contact 20 small graduate-heavy colleges (nursing, counseling). Offer a $5k cap-readiness audit reviewing 100 student files. Publish a plain-English cap guide to generate leads and sign 3.

title: Microschool Compliance Kit With Built-In Insurance
one_liner: State-by-state registration, safeguarding, ESA and scholarship vendor onboarding, records and liability insurance sold as one subscription to microschool founders.
customer: Microschool founders and learning-pod operators (10-40 students each) and microschool networks; about 1,000 microschools are reportedly in limbo awaiting federal tax-credit rules.
problem: Microschool legal status differs by state, scholarship-credit eligibility rules are unresolved, ESA vendor marketplaces are closed and painful to enter, and insurers are wary of unregulated child programs. Founders are ex-teachers and parents drowning in paperwork, and states are scrutinizing (Pennsylvania cited Alpha School for significant deficiencies).
solution: A compliance operating system: a state legal-status wizard, prefilled filings, fire and occupancy checklists, background-check and mandated-reporter workflows, attendance and records, ESA vendor applications and invoicing, and a bundled liability and abuse-and-molestation policy through an MGA partnership.
why_now: The scholarship credit begins in 2027 in 31 states, ESA programs are expanding (Texas had 200k+ applicants), and the microschool count is growing while final rules are in flux.
revenue_model: $199-399 per month per school SaaS, insurance commission of 15-20% on premiums of about $2-6k per school-year, and a $500 ESA vendor concierge fee.
non_obvious_insight: The moat is not software but insurability. Insurers will price a standardized, audited operating model far better than a random pod, and whoever accumulates loss-ratio data first sets the industry standard.
first_30_days: Pick two ESA states, build checklists and a $750 'launch audit', and sell to 20 founders through microschool founder groups. Pre-negotiate terms with an MGA or broker.

title: Extranet Takeover Defense for Independent Hotels
one_liner: Managed monitoring and fraud response for hotels' OTA extranet logins and guest-messaging channels, the credential theft that turns into guest payment scams.
customer: Independent hotels, B&Bs and small STR managers of 10-150 rooms, their channel-manager and PMS resellers, and cyber insurers.
problem: Attackers phish or infect front-desk staff, take over OTA extranet accounts and message arriving guests from the genuine booking thread asking for payment via fraudulent links. The hotel absorbs chargebacks and reputational damage and can lose OTA account standing. These hotels have no IT staff and are too small for security vendors.
solution: A light service that watches for leaked credentials tied to the hotel's domain and staff emails, alerts on suspicious extranet login emails, flags guest messages containing external links or payment requests, and runs 10-minute staff phishing training. It adds a 24/7 hotline for incident response and a guest-facing 'how we ask for payment' page.
why_now: AI-written phishing in dozens of languages, widely reported hospitality-targeted credential theft campaigns in 2025, and merchant-model payments that concentrate risk in OTA accounts. Insurers are hardening cyber requirements.
revenue_model: EUR 49-149 per property per month, insurer commissions and per-incident response fees.
non_obvious_insight: The weak node is the hotel's front-desk laptop, not the OTA platform. The unit of attack is a booking thread the guest already trusts, so simple detection at the message level gives most of the protection.
first_30_days: Run a free credential-exposure scan for 100 hotel domains using public breach data. Send each hotel its results, convert 10 to paid, and partner with two hotel associations for distribution.

title: Satellite Cannibalization Scores for Rural ISP Lenders
one_liner: Address-level risk scores that show which rural ISP portfolios LEO broadband will hollow out, and which it will not.
customer: Lenders to rural ISPs (cooperative and agricultural lenders, community banks), funds buying wireless or fiber ISPs, tower and fixed-wireless investors, and state broadband offices that allocate subsidies.
problem: Starlink went from 8.9M to 12M subscribers in six months (per the briefing) while ARPU fell 19% in one quarter. That means it is pricing down into the rural segments small ISPs live on. Lenders still underwrite these ISPs on legacy subscriber-count assumptions, and nobody can tell which locations are actually exposed.
solution: A data product that scores every serviceable location: fiber or cable alternatives, fixed wireless, LEO availability and price, local congestion, and expected churn or ARPU pressure. It rolls up to portfolio covenants, valuation adjustments and acquisition due-diligence reports. Updated monthly as satellite pricing and capacity change.
why_now: Subscriber growth of about 35% in six months, falling ARPU and satellite eligibility in subsidy programs all landed in 2025-26. Starship-driven capacity growth should push prices down further.
revenue_model: Portfolio subscription $2-10k per month per lender. $10-40k per acquisition due-diligence report. Data licensing to ISP-focused funds.
non_obvious_insight: The consensus is fiber wins and satellites lose. The actual exposure is mid-density fixed-wireless and DSL footprints, and the difference is visible at address level. Lenders get paid for knowing which side of that line each loan sits on.
first_30_days: Build a prototype on public availability maps, FCC broadband data and published Starlink plan tiers for three states. Pitch five agricultural or community lenders with a free look at one real portfolio. Convert one to a paid pilot.

title: Aftermarket Support for Stranded DJI Fleets
one_liner: Repair, rebuilt batteries, parts and firmware-independence retrofits for the many legally owned DJI drones that can no longer be replaced with new models.
customer: Police and fire drone units, agricultural spray operators, land surveyors, roofing and solar inspectors, and small public-safety departments with grant money.
problem: The FCC barred new DJI and Autel models in December 2025, US drone tariffs took effect in September 2026 (component tariffs follow in 2027), and China's export controls now cover motors, batteries, radios and sensors. Existing fleets stay legal to fly but face scarce parts and no assured US repair path.
solution: A US repair depot with stocked parts, rebuilt batteries using allied-source cells, gimbal and camera swaps, and open flight-controller retrofits (ArduPilot/PX4) as a migration path. Offer a per-drone maintenance plan with predictive service, and trade-in credits toward US-made airframes, which also become a lead source for those makers.
why_now: The December 2025 FCC action, September 2026 tariffs and export controls all landed within a year. The installed base is large and aging, and no one has a business focused on serving it.
revenue_model: $150-800 per repair, $30-80 per drone per month for maintenance plans, battery and parts sales, and referral fees from US airframe makers on trade-ins.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone debates who replaces DJI, while nobody serves the installed base for the next 5 years. Service earns higher margin than building a competing airframe, starts faster, and gives you the customer list every US-made airframe maker wants.
first_30_days: Buy 20 broken Mavic and Matrice units on secondary markets and set up a bench. Pitch fixed-price maintenance plans to 30 sheriff drone units and agricultural spraying co-ops, and sell the first 10 plans.

title: Tech-to-Owner Buyout Kit for Trade Shops
one_liner: Package and finance the sale of sub-$5M trade shops to their own senior technicians or managers, then keep them on a shared back office so the acquired shop does not stall.
customer: Retiring owners of 5-40 person HVAC, plumbing, electrical and roofing shops that PE roll-ups skip, plus their number-two techs or GMs and SBA lenders.
problem: McKinsey says 6M small businesses face ownership transitions by 2035 and a third of owners over 50 struggle to find a buyer. PE pays 10-14x EBITDA for platforms above $25M revenue but only 2-3.5x for small owner-operators, a 3-5x valuation gap. When the small shop closes, its crew and customers vanish, deepening the trades shortage.
solution: A deal factory: clean financials from QuickBooks and field-service exports, SBA 7(a) plus seller-note packaging, a 90-day transition playbook, license-qualifier continuity, and a fractional-CFO and shared back office (payroll, purchasing group, bidding) for the new owner. A short cohort teaches buyer-techs finance, hiring and pricing.
why_now: PE buying spree (Apollo/Apex, Blackstone/Champions, Bain/Service Logic) raises the visible price of scale but skips small shops. The silver-tsunami timeline is now. Roofing is the least consolidated trade and ServiceTitan is deprioritizing it, so owners have fewer software-led growth options.
revenue_model: 3-5% success fee on the deal. $2-4K per month shared back-office subscription for 24-36 months.
non_obvious_insight: The best buyer for a small shop is not PE or a stranger, it is the employee who already knows the customers, trucks and quirks. What is missing is packaging, seller financing and post-close operating support. Every closed shop deletes 5-20 tradespeople from a scarce local supply, which makes preservation valuable to the community.
first_30_days: Pick one trade in one metro. Cold-outreach 200 owners aged 58+ from state license databases with a free 30-minute valuation chat. Sign three exclusive listings, identify the tech buyers via the owners, and line up two SBA lenders.

title: AI Re-Post Radar with First-Publication Proof
one_liner: A seal-then-watch tool that timestamps a creator's work before publishing and finds AI-reworded, re-voiced copies, with a ready-to-file complaint.
customer: Educational and commentary YouTubers, podcast producers and paid-newsletter writers with 10k-500k audiences, and small MCNs that manage them.
problem: The industry argues about whether a piece is AI-made. For a creator being ripped off, the deciding fact is who published first. Faceless channels can transcribe, reword and re-voice a human video or post within hours. YouTube's Jul 16 policy on generic or repetitive content helps in principle, but enforcement depends on complaints, and long-tail creators lack Content ID-style tooling.
solution: A pre-publish 'seal' takes a hash of script, audio and footage plus an embedding of the transcript, anchored to a public timestamp log. A radar then checks YouTube, TikTok, Substack, Medium, RSS and podcast directories for semantic near-duplicates, using transcript embeddings so reworded copies still match. It scores them, and drafts a YouTube reused-content complaint, DMCA notice or EU DSA notice with the timestamp proof attached.
why_now: Rewriting and re-voicing are now nearly free, while platforms have just adopted policies that penalize repetitive content but rely on rights-holders to report. Embeddings make cheap semantic matching practical.
revenue_model: $29-99/month per creator, $5 per auto-filed takedown bundle, and agency plans for MCNs.
non_obvious_insight: Origin time beats origin type. A timestamped record survives rewording, re-encoding and watermark stripping, while 'made by AI or not' is a probabilistic argument. The evidence is the product.
first_30_days: Build a transcript-and-embedding pipeline on the YouTube Data API and Whisper, limited to each customer's niche keywords. Recruit 10 creators from YouTuber Discords and demo by finding real re-posts of their videos within the first hour. Charge $29/month after the free scan.

title: AI-Washing Forensics for Investors and Buyers
one_liner: A five-day outside-in diligence product that tests whether an AI startup's product is real autonomy, its revenue is real, and its users are human.
customer: Seed-to-growth investors (micro-VCs, corporate VCs, growth funds), corporate M&A teams, venture lenders, and enterprise procurement teams buying AI vendors.
problem: Builder.ai's 2025 insolvency (marketed AI, with heavy human labour behind it), the 2025 DOJ case against the founder of Nate, and a wave of 'ARR' made of pilots, credits and bot traffic show that diligence rests on demos, reference calls and a quality-of-earnings that never tests the technology claim.
solution: A black-box harness and data-room protocol. It covers interaction testing at scale (latency and variance signatures that reveal human-in-the-loop or third-party model calls), unit-economics reconstruction (tokens versus price versus gross margin), revenue reality (read-only Stripe and bank data plus contract sampling to separate pilot, committed, credit-funded and refunded revenue), audience authenticity (bot and agent share of users from server logs), and independent reference call-backs. Output is a 'Reality Report' with confidence intervals.
why_now: Builder.ai (2025) and Delve (2026) reset investor trust. AI-startup ARR claims are exploding, and more than half of web traffic is now automated, which inflates 'users'. Investors are compressing diligence to days, and AI products are uniquely testable from outside because you can hit the endpoint.
revenue_model: $15-40k per full report paid by the investor (often reimbursed at close), a $5k lite scan, and annual portfolio-monitoring retainers for funds.
non_obvious_insight: Insiders assume diligence must rely on the founder's data. AI products can be tested from the outside, so the scarce thing is independence and speed, and the buyer of speed is an investor with a 48-hour exclusivity window.
first_30_days: Offer five free 'reality scans' to angel syndicates and micro-VC partners on live deals in exchange for named case studies. Build the harness with two ML engineers and one forensic accountant. Set pricing after three wins.

title: Ghost-Student Fraud Defense for Community Colleges
one_liner: Enrollment-fraud screening built into admissions and financial-aid workflows that separates real applicants from bot-driven ghost students before aid disburses.
customer: Community-college districts' admissions, financial-aid and IT-security offices, plus state college systems. There are about 1,000 community colleges in the US.
problem: Fraud rings use stolen or synthetic identities, and increasingly AI-completed coursework, to enroll and collect federal and state aid. California community colleges have reported large shares of applications as fraudulent and tens of millions of dollars lost. Regulators have tightened identity-verification requirements for aid recipients. Staff are overwhelmed by manual reviews, and consumer IDV tools do not fit education workflows.
solution: Integrate with student information and learning management systems. Risk-score at application, enrollment and first-week activity using LMS login patterns, IP and ASN reuse, device farms, writing similarity and disbursement-account reuse. Send only high-risk cases to paid ID verification, place aid holds, produce OIG-ready reports, and give auditors a dashboard.
why_now: The 2025-26 ghost-student wave hit colleges as AI agents got good enough to attend and submit work, and aid-verification rules tightened. State funding for fraud response exists.
revenue_model: $25-100K per district per year, or $0.10-0.50 per application screened.
non_obvious_insight: The budget owner is financial-aid compliance, driven by audit findings and risk to aid eligibility, not IT. The best signals (LMS behavior) exist only after enrollment, so this is behavioral IDV that consumer vendors cannot copy.
first_30_days: Pilot with 2 colleges. Retro-score one semester of application logs to show dollars at risk, pitch through financial-aid and CIO associations, and price at $2K per month.

title: Designed Toxin Binders for Mouse-Free Antivenom QC
one_liner: Sequence-defined, AI-designed toxin-class binders sold as reference reagents that let antivenom makers test potency without mouse lethality assays.
customer: Antivenom manufacturers (public institutes in Latin America and India, plus private and UK/US firms), WHO and regulator working groups, toxinology labs, and funders such as Wellcome and Gates for later recombinant antivenom.
problem: WHO's 2017 guidelines say murine LD50 and ED50 lethality tests remain the only validated preclinical potency method, despite 3Rs pressure. ELISA, nAChR-binding and cytotoxicity surrogates exist but lack stable, defined, universal reagents, because animal-derived antibodies vary lot to lot.
solution: Produce designed binders for the major toxin families (three-finger toxins, PLA2, SVMP) in E. coli, following the approach in Nature (Jan 2025), where de novo proteins neutralized three-finger toxins and protected mice. Sell (1) calibrator and capture-reagent kits for competition ELISA and nAChR-competition assays, and (2) a 'toxin-family neutralization profile' service showing what each antivenom lot neutralizes, correlated to mouse ED50 over 10-20 lots. Later, co-develop recombinant cocktails.
why_now: The 2025 Nature paper proved designed proteins can neutralize venom toxins. WHO explicitly encourages alternatives. Regulators are moving toward non-animal methods (FDA's Sept 21, 2026 rule is the latest signal). AI design has made binders cheap.
revenue_model: $2-10k research-use kits, $5-20k per lot profile service, grants ($200k-2M) for validation, and later per-dose royalties on recombinant products.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone frames designed antivenom as a therapeutic moonshot. The wedge is quality control: reagents sell before regulators accept a replacement, and manufacturers already pay for mouse colonies. Sequence-defined reagents beat animal-derived ones on reproducibility. Honest caveat: first revenue is likely grants plus small reagent orders.
first_30_days: Check IP with the University of Washington and DTU or design new binders. Express three binders. Send sample sets to 2 antivenom labs for correlation on 10 lots. Apply for a small grant while selling research-use kits to toxinology labs.

title: Fish Settlement Audit Becoming the Fleet's Payment Rail
one_liner: Start by auditing settlement sheets against fish tickets to recover missed money, then become the split-pay rail that routes each settlement to crew, lessors, lenders and the IRS.
customer: Skippers and permit holders who pay $99 flat or 15% of any recovered amount for the audit. Crew use the shares calculator free. Later, skippers and quota lessors pay about 0.3-0.5% of settlement flow for split-pay, and lenders and CFEC-adjacent programs pay referral fees.
problem: The 'price' you're paid is a stack: base price, quality bonuses (for example $0.15 RSW, $0.05 bleeding, $0.05 chilling), loyalty or volume bonuses, post-season retros, and deductions for ice, fuel, gear advances and storage. Every processor's sheet looks different. The fisherman's own copy of the fish ticket sits in a Ziploc in the wheelhouse and never gets matched against the settlement. Nobody checks. Then the whole lump lands in one skipper's account weeks later and he has to act as the bank for crew shares, quota lease payments, loan payments, gear vendors and self-employment tax. That is where disputes, missed quarterly taxes and stiffed crew come from.
solution: Audit: photograph the settlement sheet and fish tickets, and an LLM parses pounds, price stack, bonuses and deductions, flags weight mismatches, missed quality bonuses, wrong grades and unexplained deductions, and prints a plain-English 'you were owed' letter. A crew shares calculator generates crew settlement sheets from the skipper's expense rules. Rail: once trust exists, route the settlement into a virtual account that auto-splits per signed crew share agreement, quota lease, loan payments, vendor invoices and a tax set-aside, with instant partial payments.
why_now: Final settlements for the 2026 salmon season are landing right now (Oct-Dec). Price swung from $1.03 to $1.72 in one year, so fishermen are checking. Vision LLMs can read messy sheets at near-zero cost. Banking-as-a-service and real-time payment rails make split-pay possible for a small team. Crew who waited about four years for crab disaster relief also learned that clean earnings paperwork is worth money.
revenue_model: Audit: $99 flat or 15% of recovery. Rail: 0.3-0.5% of settlement flow plus interchange and float. Later: earned-wage advances against booked settlements, lender referrals, claim-packet prep for federal disaster relief (crew earnings vaults double as the proof), and an anonymized price tape sold to buyers and lenders.
non_obvious_insight: The skipper is the fleet's unlicensed bank, and nobody has both documents in one place. The audit is the trojan horse: it gets a fisherman to hand over settlement history, which is exactly the underwriting and routing data needed for the rail. The settlement sheet is a stack of price components, and the money is hidden in the parts nobody reads.
first_30_days: Post in fishermen's Facebook groups: 'free settlement check, send the sheet.' Process 100 sheets by hand plus LLM, log every error found, and turn 5-10 recoveries into case studies. Build the crew share calculator as a free viral wedge. Charge 15% of recovered amounts above $500. Start collecting the anonymized price stack by port, species and processor.

title: Monetization Compliance-as-Code for Free-to-Play Studios
one_liner: A linter that reads a studio's store and gacha configuration and flags per-country, per-age-band violations, with an auditable rulebook curated by counsel.
customer: Mid-size free-to-play mobile and PC studios and publishers (10-300 staff) selling in the EU, UK, Brazil, Australia and US states.
problem: Rules diverge fast. Brazil's 2025 child-protection law restricts loot boxes for minors (in force in 2026), the EU consumer authorities set 2025 principles on virtual currency pricing, and an EU Digital Fairness Act proposal is expected around late 2026. Roblox age tiers and Discord age checks add age-band segmentation. Studios rely on $400-600 per hour legal memos and hand-checked spreadsheets.
solution: Ingest offer tables, gacha odds, currency bundles and subscription flows from LiveOps exports or APIs. Flag violations per market and age band against a versioned rulebook, produce audit-ready evidence, and gate builds in CI.
why_now: Brazil's restrictions took effect in 2026, the Digital Fairness Act is in the pipeline, and platform age tiers force age-aware storefronts. Enforcement history (Epic's FTC settlements) shows the cost of missing this.
revenue_model: $500-3,000 per month per title, $5-15k onboarding, and a premium tier with counsel-reviewed rule updates.
non_obvious_insight: Games compliance is sold as legal advice, but violations live in JSON: drop tables, prices, labels and flows. That is machine-checkable, law firms sell memos, and nobody ships a linter.
first_30_days: Have a games-regulatory lawyer co-write a 4-market rulebook. Build a linter for one config format (Remote Config plus a gacha CSV). Offer free audits to 10 mobile studios and convert 2 to $1k per month.

title: Government Property Control Kit for New Defense Makers
one_liner: A fixed-price property-system-in-a-box (tags, procedures, mock audit, reconciliation) that keeps first-time defense manufacturers from failing their government property audit and having payments withheld.
customer: New-entrant defense manufacturers (drone, munitions second-source and component startups) and small machine shops that receive government-furnished property, plus primes that flow the property clauses down and want their subs certified.
problem: Contractors holding government-furnished property must run a property management system with receiving reports, physical inventory, loss and damage reporting, and reconciliation to the contract's property list. If the government disapproves the system, contracting officers can direct payment withholds. Small shops run this on spreadsheets and no one is the accountable hand-receipt holder. Property administrators cannot coach, and consultants bill $200-400 an hour.
solution: A packaged offering. A one-day on-site 'mock property system analysis' run by former property administrators. Asset tagging and mobile scanning. Templated procedures, forms and a monthly reconciliation to the contract property list. Audit-ready binder and annual physical inventory support. Ongoing loss/damage/destruction reporting and excess-property disposition paperwork. Position it to program managers, not compliance officers, as schedule protection.
why_now: The Revolutionary FAR Overhaul rewrote Part 45 (Government Property), with model deviation text implemented from November 2025, so many contractors are rereading their obligations. Defense spending and drone and munitions ramp-ups are pulling venture-backed hardware companies and first-time subs into contracts with government-furnished property. CMMC phase-ins compete for the same small compliance budgets, so property control gets ignored until an audit finds it.
revenue_model: Mock audit at $6-15k, then $500-2,000 a month for software plus fractional property-officer support, plus per-asset tagging fees. Prime-sponsored programs where a prime pays to certify its sub base.
non_obvious_insight: The property system is about 90% behavior and 10% software: who signs for what, and whether there is an unbroken trail from receipt to disposition. Auditors find the same handful of deficiencies again and again (no receiving report, no physical inventory, no reconciliation, no loss report), so a checklist-driven fixed-price service works better than custom consulting. The strongest sponsor is the prime, because a sub's disapproved system threatens the prime's own schedule and cash.
first_30_days: Pull first-time awardees from SBIR/STTR winners and public contract awards that carry government-furnished property. Offer 10 of them a $2,500 one-day GFP health check. Publish a one-page 'seven findings auditors keep writing' as lead magnet. Partner with a regional APEX Accelerator for referrals and a CMMC registered provider organization for cross-sell. Turn the first 3 engagements into a templated binder and a simple scanning workflow before building any software.

title: Borrowing-Base Verification for Recycler Lenders
one_liner: A drone-and-assay 'borrowing base as a service' that lets specialty lenders finance recyclers against verified inventory.
customer: Asset-based lenders, factoring firms and specialty commodity funds (primary payers), plus recyclers who need working capital against bales, black mass, swarf and scrap.
problem: After Ascend's Chapter 11, Li-Cycle's bankruptcy and the PET reclaimer closures, credit for recyclers is tight. Lenders cannot verify what is in the pile: volume, grade, moisture, title and price risk. Commodity-finance frauds, shrink and theft are a real concern.
solution: Monthly drone and LiDAR volumetrics, density and grade sampling, scale-house data integration, title and lien checks, and index-based mark-to-market. Lender-ready certificates with shrink alerts.
why_now: The 2025-26 recycling failures made lenders cautious, while BIS-driven domestic feed flows and price volatility make inventory more valuable and more mispriced.
revenue_model: $1.5-4K per site per month, plus basis points on facilities placed.
non_obvious_insight: Recyclers are not short of collateral; lenders are short of trust in it. Collateral management firms serve large metal traders and skip the $5-50M recyclers.
first_30_days: Talk to 10 ABL lenders and 2 factoring firms. Pilot with 3 recyclers refinancing now. Build a volumetrics pipeline on off-the-shelf drones and photogrammetry.

title: Agentic Crypto Trace-and-Freeze Desk for Police
one_liner: An AI forensic analyst that traces a victim's stolen crypto across chains in minutes and drafts freeze requests, sold to local police who receive these reports but cannot trace.
customer: Police and sheriff's fraud and elder-crimes units, state AG consumer units, victim-service nonprofits and credit unions.
problem: Crypto-related complaints hit 181,565 and $11.4B in 2025, and victims report to local police who lack $20K+ blockchain forensics tools and training. Funds hop through swaps, bridges and exchange deposit addresses, and freeze windows are measured in hours.
solution: An officer or victim enters a transaction hash and an agent traces flows across major chains and bridges, clusters to exchange deposit addresses using open labels, and produces a freeze packet (evidence PDF and correctly formatted requests to exchange law-enforcement portals and stablecoin issuers). The officer approves, and recovery outcomes are tracked.
why_now: Tool-using agents can now run chain-analysis workflows and draft legal requests. Stablecoin issuers are cooperating on freezes at scale, and scam flows concentrate in a few tokens and exchanges.
revenue_model: $3-10K per agency per year, or about $150 per case, with elder-justice grant funding.
non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck in crypto recovery is procedural delivery, not analytics: which desk accepts what format, and how fast. An agent that sends the right request in minutes matters more than another dashboard.
first_30_days: Build tracing for USDT on Tron and Ethereum plus Bitcoin to the top 10 exchanges. Offer free traces to 10 sheriff's offices, track freezes, publish outcomes, and start $250 per month pilots with elder-justice grant funding lined up.
